title: Australia 2-4 Brazil: Raphinha and Vinicius score penalties in absorbing Brisbane friendly
subtitle: Following a 1-1 draw between the teams last Friday, Brazil got the better of Australia in a six-goal thriller to cap their tour Down Under.
paragraphs: Raphinha and Vinicius Junior were both on target from the penalty spot as Brazil beat Australia 4-2 in a thrilling friendly encounter in Brisbane.

Carlo Ancelotti made seven changes to the Selecao lineup that drew 1-1 with the same opponents in Townsville four days prior, but three of those who kept their places – Raphinha, Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes – got on the scoresheet in an entertaining win.

Brazil had to wait until the 95th minute for Rayan's equaliser on Friday, but they made the breakthrough far quicker this time around as Vanderson's touch sat up perfectly for the full-back to thump a volley across Patrick Beach and in with three minutes gone, after Gabriel Bontempo laid the ball back into his path.
Beach then repelled two efforts from Raphinha as Brazil's furious start threatened to overwhelm Australia, but the hosts grew into the encounter and equalised in the 28th minute.

Connor Metcalfe's inswinging corner somehow travelled all the way through to Alessandro Circati, who hooked his right foot behind him and sent an instinctive flick looping into the far corner. Referee Yusuke Araki initially awarded a foul on Brazil goalkeeper Otavio, but a VAR review led to that decision being overturned.
And the Socceroos were ahead only five minutes later, as a flowing move resulted in Metcalfe exchanging passes with Circati and sending a glorious, 20-yard strike dipping into the top-right corner.
However, Brazil got back on level terms just before half-time, with Raphinha planting his spot-kick into the bottom-right corner after Danilo Santos was tripped by Harry Soutter.

And, after Gabriel Magalhaes' header was kept out by Beach, Guimaraes put Brazil back in front in the 69th minute, sweeping into a gaping net after Vinicius linked up with his Real Madrid team-mate Endrick in the left-hand channel.

Another driving run from Vinicius led to him being felled by Nestory Irankunda, and with Raphinha having been substituted at half-time, the Madrid superstar became the second Brazilian to convert from the spot 10 minutes from time, finally putting the game out of Australia's reach.
Vinicius leads the way, but defensive issues remain for Brazil
Ancelotti's side were far from their free-flowing best at this summer's World Cup, as they were beaten by Norway in the round of 16.
And after Australia came within seconds of upsetting them in the first of two friendly matches between the sides, the Italian came in for more criticism from the Brazilian media.
However, his side looked much brighter in attack on Tuesday, putting up 3.62 expected goals from 18 shots, compared to Australia's 1.65 xG from eight attempts.

Vinicius was at the heart of everything positive about Brazil's play, tallying game-high figures for dribbles attempted (four), touches in the opposition area (seven) and chances created (two, joint with Bontempo).

Brazil still have defensive issues to solve ahead of Saturday's meeting with India, though. This was the first instance of Australia both scoring and conceding multiple goals before half-time in any game since a 2-2 draw with Saudi Arabia in June 2017.
The Socceroos also become just the second team from the AFC confederation to score twice against Brazil in a game in the last 21 years, after Japan beat the Selecao 3-2 last October.
